Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Clinical triage summarization for intake notes (short summaries + risk flags).
- Strong refusal/safety behavior for PHI and sensitive instructions (must never hallucinate diagnoses or provide treatment advice).
- Low-latency inference for front-line triage UI (p95 < 350ms target).
- Ability to run evals on a representative sample and iterate on prompts/policy.

Immediate next steps (what I’ll do):
1) Share a short list of recommended model variants to try (low-cost/small to higher-capacity) + quantization options.
2) Share a link to a benchmark/repro harness we can run on your sample data.
3) Provide a safety/refusal prompt set we use for policy behavior evals and some example outputs.

What I need from you:
- A 200–500 message sample set (de-identified) or a synthetic sample if PHI prohibits sharing.
- Confirmation of any regulatory constraints (e.g., regional data residency, specific controls).

I’ll get the model recs and benchmark link to you by tomorrow EOD PST. If it helps, we can book a 45-minute technical deep-dive with Dev and Ethan to walk through the eval harness and safety tests next week.

High-level model recommendations (summary from the PDF):
- redwood-instruct-1.2-7b (best balance of instruction following + safety; recommend 8-bit quant for Dedicated)

- For safety behavior we surface: refusal rates, false-positives (overrefusal), and hallucinatory assertions.

Data/security: for Dedicated/Private deployments we support:
- Customer-managed VPC + KMS/HSM integration for keying;
- Configurable retention/ephemeral caching;
- SOC 2 and audit logs (I’ve linked our compliance summary in the Drive link Marissa shared).
